pattern.short_summary: More than one party is present at the same system instance at the same time — two humans, a dyad, a group, or humans plus a population of agents — and the design allocates distinct roles among them.
pattern.definition: More than one party is present at the same system instance at the same time — two humans, a dyad, a group, or humans plus a population of agents — and the design allocates distinct roles among them. The system is addressed to the configuration rather than to a single user.
pattern.structural_signature: At least two simultaneous role slots on one system instance, each with its own input rights, and system behavior that depends on which role acted. Removing one participant leaves the interaction structurally incomplete — a role goes unfilled — rather than merely reducing the number of users.

dimension.category_description: How human and artificial participants are personified, assigned visible roles, coordinated, simulated, or represented to one another.
dimension.classification_boundary: Identity or social organization must be user-facing; invisible multi-agent division of labor is excluded.
